data.narrative:
Hexana is a seed-stage nuclear energy company founded by Sylvain Nizou and Paul Gauthe that has raised €25M to date. The valuation exercise draws from a comp universe of 11 private and 3 public peers in the nuclear energy sector, including private companies such as Nano Nuclear Energy, Oklo, Valar Atomics, X-Energy, and Fuse Energy, alongside public equities OKLO, NNE, and SMR.

The stage-progression method is the primary applicable triangulation approach. Using the €25M raised as a valuation proxy and applying a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier between seed and subsequent stages yields an implied valuation of €62M. This method is grounded in observed capital step-ups at the seed-to-Series A transition in the nuclear technology space.

Peer-median analysis is not applicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables; only one same-stage and one adjacent-stage peer exist within the narrow nuclear energy seed cohort, below the three-datapoint threshold required for statistical confidence. A broader all-sector median would introduce unwarranted noise. The triangulation supports a valuation range of €53M (low) to €72M (high), with a median point of €62M. Key uncertainties include the appropriateness of the 2.5x multiplier given nuclear energy's longer development cycles relative to software and biotech benchmarks, and the absence of direct peer valuation anchors at identical stage and capital levels.
